title: Install the manufacturing module shell (mes_core) in a company
description: A tenant administrator installs the mes_core module in their own company, with a written reason. The module is an empty shell today: it brings the module record and its four dependencies check, and no screens, routes, permissions, roles or handlers. Installing it is the tenant administrator's own act; no company gets it automatically.
preconditions: the modules org, catalog_items, locations, codes and stock are installed in the company (mes_core declares catalog_items, locations, org and stock as dependencies)
the administrator signs in to the company's own address

tasks.result: the module record mes_core 0.1.0 is created in the company (201); the company gets no new screen, route or permission

outputs: the mes_core module record of the company (version 0.1.0)
refusals: no rationale or a blank one: 422 'rationale is required'
a dependency not installed: 422 'missing dependency: <id>' and nothing is installed

title: Security: the install of mes_core is refused without its dependencies and does not leak to another company
description: Negative process (D-170). Installing mes_core in a company that lacks a dependency is refused and installs nothing; installing it in one company leaves every other company without it.
preconditions: two companies A and B; in A the dependencies are installed, in B they are not

tasks.result: B's administrator gets 422 missing dependency and mes_core is not installed in B
after A installs mes_core, B still has no mes_core record

refusals: install in A does not create a record in B (schema-per-tenant)

title: Security: who may install or remove the module (permission matrix of the module-management routes)
description: Negative process (D-170). The module-management routes (install, settings, uninstall, reactivate, upgrade, rollback, ensure-seeds) need ModulesManage. mes_core adds no permission and no role grant, so the matrix for it is the core matrix: only TENANT_ADMIN (in its company) and PLATFORM_ADMIN hold ModulesManage; every other role, a missing credential and a wrong credential are refused.
preconditions: the golden permission matrix of the product (priv/permission_matrix/effective.golden)

tasks.result: 403 for a role without ModulesManage; nothing changes (planned as a runner step: the matrix is read from the golden file, the HTTP refusal is not yet scripted)

title: Security: MES data paths (crafted writes, cross-company reads, token and host, uploads, webhooks, approval) -- not buildable yet
description: Negative processes required by D-170 for the MES data paths: crafted completion or start refused (write targets), a token of company A against company B's ids answered with a uniform 404, the permission matrix per role of the area, wrong/expired/other-company token and unknown host, upload types and limits, old-address access, voice and webhook inputs, approval and separation of duties. Today mes_core has no routes, screens, handlers, permissions, roles, uploads, webhooks or approval steps, so each of these is PLANNED: it becomes a real process when plan tasks M2..M11 (docs/design/mes/13-phase1-plan.md) add the thing it tests. Until then there is nothing to refuse, and none of them is automated.
refusals: crafted completion/start of a MES step: planned, 422 output_refused expected (needs M-tasks with write handlers)
cross-company read and write: planned, uniform 404 expected (needs M-tasks with routes)
permission matrix per MES role (operator, shift lead, QC analyst, QA releaser): planned (plan task M10)
token and host lookup, upload types and limits, old-address access, voice/webhook inputs, approval and separation of duties: planned, no such function exists in mes_core
requirement: none yet: MES plan tasks M2..M11 in docs/design/mes/13-phase1-plan.md have no REQ entry in docs/requirements.yaml
